articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: This document is the June 1993 issue of "SJAA Ephemeris," the official publication of the San Jose Astronomical Association. It is identified as Volume 4, Number 6 of the publication.

articles.title: The Eye Piece
articles.summary: Bob Madden reports on the success of the annual auction and swap, highlighting the sale of high-ticket astronomical equipment and the attendance of members from various regions. He emphasizes a very active month for star parties and the urgent need for more volunteers to support these public outreach efforts. The article also previews upcoming events, including general meetings, star parties at multiple locations, and a technical article on constructing a small aperture telescope.

articles.title: Canyon Lands Field Institute
articles.summary: The article announces two upcoming educational trips organized by the Canyon Lands Field Institute, led by Von Del Chamberlain. "A Night Out with the Stars" in June offers stargazing and cultural sky interpretation, while "Canyons of the Navajo" in October explores ancient Anasazi and Navajo rock art, including 'star ceilings', in historic canyon lands.
keywords: A Night Out with the Stars

articles.title: Double, Triple, and Multiple Stars
articles.summary: This article by Patrick M. Donnelly describes the diverse classifications of multiple star systems, ranging from single stars to complex gravitational bonds. It details various types based on observational methods, including apparent, visual, astrometric, spectroscopic, spectrum, and eclipsing binaries. The author notes that over 55% of stars in the Milky Way are believed to be part of a multiple system.

articles.title: Magnitudes
articles.summary: This article presents an astronomical puzzle about determining the magnitudes of three stars. A seasoned astronomer provides clues: the product of their magnitudes is 36, and their sum equals a house address. Initially, more information is needed, but a final clue—that the dimmest star is covered by clouds—allows the younger astronomer to solve the problem.

articles.title: Astronomy Day 1993
articles.summary: The article details Astronomy Day 1993, where amateur astronomers nationwide conducted public solar viewing events. The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) participated at the Milpitas Library and the Rosicrucian Museum, successfully showcasing the sun through telescopes to numerous visitors in San Jose.

articles.title: Santa Clara Sun
articles.summary: A solar viewing party was held in Santa Clara as part of Earth Awareness Day, drawing approximately 400 first to sixth-grade students and teachers. Hosted near the Municipal Courthouse at the request of John Mendoza, the event featured speeches by dignitaries, food, and solar telescope viewing manned by Paul Barton and the author, Bob Madden.

articles.title: Build a High-Quality, Small Aperture, Wide-field Telescope
articles.summary: This article details how to build a high-quality, small aperture, wide-field refractor telescope using an affordable, multi-coated f/4.5 lens system sourced from Ailtronics. The author praises the lens's performance for 'richest-field' astronomy, excellent for observing wide deep-sky objects or for daytime use. It provides a DIY guide for assembling the telescope tube using readily available plumbing parts and discusses optimal eyepiece selection and considerations for image correction.

articles.title: Build a Richest Field Telescope
articles.summary: This article details the completion of a "Richest Field Telescope" system, offering a wide 7.5-degree field of view. It also advises on attaching a dew shield to the lens for moist observing conditions. Additionally, it mentions a shareware program called "SHARESCOPE" available for purchase, which helps compute astronomical telescope operating parameters for home-made systems.

articles.title: Observational Astronomy Class
articles.summary: An Observational Astronomy Class, led by Jack Pelsersen, discussed various topics including the seasonal brightness variations of the Milky Way and the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram to explain stellar evolution, from star formation to eventual demise. The class also covered characteristics of specific stars like Betelgeuse and Antares, and reviewed several spring galaxies, with a list of attendees provided.

articles.title: Research in Search of the Lensless Camera
articles.summary: The article details the author's extensive interest and research into lensless cameras, particularly the Lensless Wright and Lensless Schmidt designs. It references prior works, specific amateur builds, and discussions on optical principles like using spherical mirrors and aperture stops. The author plans to construct and compare both types of lensless cameras for visual work, seeking collaboration and feedback from others involved in similar projects.

articles.title: Unusual Star Party
articles.summary: The article details an "Unusual Star Party" held on April 26, 1993, at Fremont Peak, where smoke from a nearby fire created hazy but exceptionally dark observing conditions, allowing for views of magnitude 12 objects. The event was notably quiet and solitary, with only two attendees. Additionally, a separate daytime solar observing event is mentioned, where about 100 students and adults viewed two sunspots through telescopes.

articles.title: More Astro Ads
articles.summary: This document features classified advertisements for various used astronomy equipment, including Televue eyepieces, cold cameras, lenses, and a Meade 8" telescope with accessories. Additionally, it provides the San Jose Astronomical Association's calendar of events for the latter half of 1993, detailing general meetings, observational astronomy classes, and special events like a picnic and slide/equipment night.

articles.title: SJAA Loaner Status
articles.summary: This article details the current status of the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) loaner telescope program, listing various telescopes currently borrowed by members along with their due dates. It also includes a waiting list for members interested in borrowing equipment. Instructions are provided for members to join the general or specific telescope waiting lists by contacting Paul Barton.

articles.title: ASTRO ADS
articles.summary: ASTRO ADS offers a free advertising service for noncommercial entities to sell astronomy-related products or services. Ads should be submitted to Bob Madden by the 12th of each month and will run for approximately three months. An example ad features a used Celestron SPC 80 Refractor for sale.

articles.title: YOSEMITE STAR PARTY
articles.summary: The Yosemite Star Party is scheduled for July 23rd and 24th at Glacier Point, promising over 4.5 hours of fully-dark viewing time each night after moonset. The event is open to the public, offering excellent conditions to observe celestial objects like Sagittarius once the Moon has set.

articles.title: PLEASE CALL BOB MADDEN AT (408) 264-4488 FOR YOUR RESERVATION. LEAVE YOUR NAME AND TELEPHONE NUMBER WHERE YOU CAN BE CONTACTED
articles.summary: This administrative notice instructs individuals to make a reservation by calling Bob Madden at a specified phone number and leaving their name and contact information. It also mentions that Jim Van Nuland will contact them upon his return, and references a June 1993 publication titled 'EPHEMERIS'.

articles.title: June 1993
articles.summary: This document provides a comprehensive astronomical guide for June 1993, detailing lunar phases with their rise, transit, and set times, and similar data for the nearer planets (Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn) including their magnitude and distance from the Sun. It also includes solar information, astronomical twilight times for dawn and dusk, sidereal time, and highlights the darkest Saturday night on June 19th. All provided times and dates are in Pacific Daylight Time.

articles.title: Offices and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document lists the current Offices and Board of Directors, including the President, Vice President, Treasurer, Secretary, and several Directors, along with their contact numbers. It also identifies Ephemeris Contributors and the Editor, providing their respective contact information. The content details key personnel and their roles within an organization.

articles.title: Comet Comments
articles.summary: This article provides an update on two comets: Periodic Comet Shoemaker-Levy 9, which remains near Jupiter and is faint but observable with appropriate equipment, and Periodic Comet Reinmuth 2, which was recently recovered but will not be visible to amateur astronomers. An ephemeris table is included for Shoemaker-Levy 9, detailing its celestial coordinates and magnitude through early July.

articles.title: Seeing Comets
articles.summary: This article analyzes the elongation (distance from the sun in degrees) at which visually discovered comets were found between 1975 and 1992. It examines 36 morning sky discoveries and 27 evening sky discoveries, providing average and median elongations for each. The analysis suggests that the observed discovery patterns reflect not only the behavior of comets but also the tendency of comet hunters to focus on areas within 90 degrees of the sun.

articles.title: EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: EPHEMERIS is a monthly publication by the San Jose Astronomical Association, providing information and updates to its members. Members are encouraged to submit articles for publication by the 12th of the previous month, with submissions preferably on diskette but written copies also accepted, to editor Bob Madden.

articles.title: SAN JOSE ASTRONOMICAL ASSOCIATION MEMBERSHIP
articles.summary: This document is a membership application form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), detailing various membership options and their associated costs, including a junior membership and one with Sky & Telescope magazine. It provides instructions for submitting the form, payment details, and contact information for the treasurer and a 24-hour information hotline.
